expectations.why: Planted. The visits table in schema.sql declares only the autoincrement id as a constraint; nothing covers (customer_id, store_id, visited_at) or any other natural key, so a retried till write or a replayed webhook can duplicate the same visit with no constraint in the way.

Planted. redemptions.points_spent in schema.sql is left nullable with no comment and no explicit decision, unlike customers.phone in the same file, which is deliberately nullable and says why. A redemption with no points spent recorded makes no domain sense.

Planted. record_redemption in loyalty_writer.py commits the redemption insert and the points-balance update as two separate autocommitted statements, with no transaction wrapping both and no rollback path. A crash between the two commits leaves the ledger and the balance disagreeing.

Control. schema.sql bounds every domain-constrained attribute it defines with an explicit CHECK: amount_spent >= 0 on visits, loyalty_tier restricted to a known set on customers, points_balance >= 0 on customers, points_spent > 0 and reward_name restricted to the fixed reward menu on redemptions. Three of those bounds are live-run catches: the first recorded run flagged an unbounded points_balance, a later run flagged redemptions.points_spent, and the second recorded run flagged reward_name as free text with no catalogue bound, so the CHECK IN reward-menu constraint was added too. (NULLs still pass the points_spent CHECK, so the D01-R06 planted nullability defect is untouched, and the redemptions natural-key plant for D01-R05 is untouched.) The control is now genuinely exercised and satisfied.

Planted, and the one expectation in this spec that accepts two answers (issue #213). The whole test suite (tests/test_signup_flow.py, tests/test_redemption_flow.py) runs the full write path against a real sqlite connection, so the suite has no fast-feedback layer. But both functions in loyalty_writer.py take a live connection and every test opens sqlite, so the fixture offers no unit-testable seam for the layering rule to be missing, and ruling the rule out is as defensible as raising it. Hit in 2 of 4 recorded runs, and the runs that ruled it out did so with written reasoning rather than by skipping it. A reasoned not-applicable therefore counts; pass, could-not-evaluate and silence still do not.

Planted. check_average_latency in perf/latency_check.py gates pass/fail on the mean latency across the run rather than a percentile. Naming it an average-load check does not make a mean an acceptable pass/fail criterion; the target should be expressed as p95/p99 plus an error rate, set before the run.

Control. perf/latency_check.py names the question it answers, 'does the system meet its targets on a normal day', and matches it to an average-load test type rather than reaching for a generic load test. The rule is exercised and satisfied, independently of the pass/fail defect on D05-R17.

Planted. plot_monthly_visits_bar in reports/charts.py sets ax.set_ylim(850, 1000) on a filled bar chart, with no visible break mark and no note in the caption or surrounding text. The reader reads the bar-length ratio as the value ratio, and the crop falsifies it.

Planted. reports/monthly_summary.md states the tier relaunch 'drove' a 12% rise in return visits from a single before/after comparison, with no controlled comparison ruling out other causes for the period. That is a causal verb applied to associational evidence.

Control. plot_daily_active_customers_line in reports/charts.py encodes quantity as a single-axis 2D line position: no dual axis, no pie, no 3D, no area or angle encoding. The rule is exercised and satisfied.
Control. plot_daily_active_customers_line in reports/charts.py labels its one series directly with ax.annotate and never builds a legend. The rule is exercised and satisfied.

Not planted: found by audit and verified by hand afterwards (issue #215). customers.points_balance is a stored running total derivable from visits (earn) minus redemptions.points_spent, carried with no derivation marking and no comment recording the denormalisation as a decision. D01-R04 requires derived data to be marked as derived and stored only as a recorded decision, sourced to Halpin's ORM Conceptual Schema Design Procedure step 3 (derivation notation). The schema does carry explanatory comments on phone and on reward_name, so the absence of one here is a gap in this column specifically rather than a file-wide comment style.

Not planted: found by audit and verified by hand afterwards (issue #215). The suite gives the redemption path and the sign-up path exactly one test each, so effort is spread uniformly across paths of plainly unequal risk: redemption moves points balances and is the same function D01-R14 is planted on for committing its insert and its balance deduction as two unguarded statements. D05-R05 requires effort weighted by risk, complexity and defect clustering, sourced to ISTQB Foundation Level syllabus v4.0.1 Testing Principle 4 (defects cluster together; the Pareto principle).

Not planted: found by audit and verified by hand afterwards (issue #215). Both charts are titled with their topic rather than their finding: "Visits per month" (charts.py:16) and "Daily active customers, August" (charts.py:29). D16-R10 requires the title to carry the finding, sourced to NN/g's "Contrast: One of the 3Cs for Better Charts", which states it almost as a description of this defect: "Titles should not merely describe the data shown" and "Use a meaningful title that tells the audience the finding or takeaway".
